text: If $\lambda$ is a dominant integral weight, then the Verma module $M(\lambda)$ is irreducible.
explanation: False: precisely when $\lambda$ is dominant integral, $M(\lambda)$ is reducible — it has a maximal proper submodule $N(\lambda)$, and the quotient $L(\lambda) = M(\lambda)/N(\lambda)$ is the finite-dimensional irreducible of highest weight $\lambda$. Verma irreducibility instead requires $\lambda+\rho$ to avoid the Weyl-shifted dominant locus.
